thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1: eu-central-1 API 5xx surge — alerting 3+ mins. spikes in gen and embed paths. request rate doubled, 5xx% 12% (5m).

sara (oncall): grabbing it. looking at top error types. tagging @mike for infra assist.

mike: on my way. quick check — provider A (gcp-europe-west1) nodes showing GPU OOMs and long queue depth on the serving pool. KV cache pressure on tails.

jonah: stack traces show `OOM when allocating tensor` and a lot of `503 backend_busy`. could be batching hitting limit.

lee: customer impact matrix from metrics: ~22 tenants in EU experiencing 10-30% failed requests for completions; embeddings failures ~6 tenants with full request failures. latency p99 doubled for long seqs.

katie-cse: getting inbound from a large EU customer — they see failed requests and timeouts. asking if there will be an SLA hit.

sara (oncall): initial mitigation plan: 1) apply conservative global rate limit for free/low-tier tenants in eu to reduce load 2) throttle long-completion (>2k tokens) requests 3) reroute new traffic to us-east fallback provider pool for critical customers only 4) start draining eu-serving nodes for reparging. agree?

mike: agree. I'll push routing weight change and apply rate-limit via envoy. commands: 
```
# reduce weight for eu pool
curl -XPOST https://routing.internal/api/adjust-weight -d '{"pool":"eu-serving","weight":0.35}'
# set per-tenant token rate limit for free tier
curl -XPOST https://quota.internal/tenants/throttle -d '{"tier":"free","rate":0.5}'
```

jonah: I'll apply a temporary `completion_token_cap=2000` for non-enterprise to prevent huge tails. Also enabling KV cache eviction to free memory.

ops-bot: Deploy started: routing-weight-change -> canary on 3 nodes. Build: rwd-router@v2.14. ETA 45s.

sara (oncall): while canary runs, mike — also flip provider fallback for premium customers to provider B (azure-eu) for new sessions. keep existing sessions sticky.

mike: done. `provider-reroute` tag applied to premium routes. logs: `reroute 124 sessions -> provider-b`

support-bot: Notifying affected customers group for EU with templated message. katie-cse please review.

katie-cse: LGTM. emphasize we are throttling non-critical features and working on rollback timeline.

jonah: can we do partial brownout instead of full drain? suggestion: disable streaming/chunked responses for free-tier in eu + postpone non-blocking background reranks.

sara (oncall): good call — partial brownout to avoid total outage. actions: - disable streaming on free/low-tier in eu - patch routing to route embeddings for enterprise only to eu, others to us-east - start graceful drain of 6 problematic nodes (1 pod at a time)

mike: draining nodes now: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data node-x` one-by-one. monitoring queue depth.

ops-bot: Canary routing and rate-limits are live. Observability: 5xx% trending down to 6% in canary slice; overall still 9%. Continue.

lee: update on customer impact: after rate limits + brownout, failed requests dropped for most tenants to <5% within 12 mins. Embeddings still routed out causing slight latency bump but functional.

katie-cse: sent initial status email to 15 flagged customers. Waiting on PR for more precise ETA.

mike: FYI, provider B capacity is limited; we've put backpressure so only premium gets rerouted. If traffic continues to surge we'll need to expand dedicated capacity or further restrict non-critical routes.

jonah: adding temporary safeguard: `reject_if_queue_depth>500` on eu-serving nodes to force earlier fallback.

sara (oncall): summary of live mitigations applied: 1) per-tenant free-tier token rate limit 50% 2) token cap 2000 for non-enterprise completions 3) disable streaming for non-premium in eu 4) routed premium new sessions to provider B 5) started graceful drain of 6 nodes 6) partial brownout of background reranks

sara (oncall): handoff plan: I'm going offline in 20m. @mike you take second-shift oncall for next 2 hours, monitor metrics and customer escalations. I'll leave runbook link: https://internal.runbooks/replay/evac-eu-2025

mike: taking over. I'll keep the thread updated. next steps: watch 5xx, p99 latency, provider B error rates, and scale up dedicated reserved pool if needed.

support-bot: Post-update sent to customers: "We applied temporary mitigations to restore service while we remediate root cause. We will follow up with timeline and postmortem."

sara (oncall): note for postmortem: owner = @jonah, timeline capture needed, root-cause hypothesis: batching + caching policy regression + provider node memory leak.

jonah: will own postmortem. collecting logs and sample traces. tagging infra and runtime teams.

mike: final note — we avoided full region failover; opted for partial brownout + targeted reroute. Recommend follow-up: schedule capacity add for provider B, run stress test on eu-serving batch scheduler, and tighten batching thresholds.

incident-bot: Incident P1 status: mitigations applied. next update scheduled 30m. :white_check_mark:
